newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil- Firmer in line with crude gains.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil- Firmer in line with crude gains.

text.p: Firm crude values boosted sentiment in the high sulphur fuel oil market on Monday with active bids and offers but sufficient supplies limit the upward momentum, traders said.
The 180-cst grade was traded at $99 and $99.50 per tonne for lifting April 1-5 and April 11-15 respectively, traders said.
Suppliers were heard to offer the 180-cst grade down from an earlier $100.50 while bids went up from $98.50.
The 180-cst grade was traded at $98 per tonne on Friday and offered at $98-$101 per tonne in the past week.
At least two arbitrage cargoes are coming from the Mediterranean and should arrive in the second half of April, said one trader.
The trader noted that several majors had built up stocks in their oil terminals, after seeing only a few buyers last week. He added that incoming Mediterranean cargoes would add pressure to prices.
European traders have estimated around 250,000 tonnes of fuel oil being worked from the Mediterranean for eastwards trips, mainly destined for Singapore, since the beginning of March.
Prices for the 3.5-percent sulphur fuel oil in the Mediterranean were close to $76 free-on-board Med bais and freight costs were about $12.50 a tonne, they said.

However, traders in Singapore agreed that prices should be supported by firm crude values as well as potential demand from a local trading company which had been supporting gas oil and fuel oil prices in the past two weeks.
The firm fuel oil swaps also helped boost sentiment, traders said. April swaps were last quoted at $98.00/$99.00 and April at $96.50/$97.50.
(Prices in dollars per tonne, unless stated)
